rubric.note: UNCHANGED: ac21f3b changed only the gilt albedo for this room. The GLB is byte-identical in size (801608), the generator diff is the gilt constant and the frames show the same geometry. Every structural point from the previous review is still open. The room is the same 8x12x5 m box with the furnace plinth dead centre. The well is still lidded: in p5-rooms-gear-shaft-void.jpg (2x crop voidtop.png) the drive shaft ends in a cap disc under red plank boards at the top of the well, so the shaft stops inside the room and does not read as climbing out of view. There are still no galleries, stair or stacked levels at chamber height. Correction to the previous note: at this hero camera the crown gear does not fully plug the hole. The upper gear pair, the gallery rail and the stone well wall above it all read in hero.jpg (crop gears.png). From the ring camera the crown gear's 2.0 m rim still fills most of the opening.

The three-gear train, the railed gallery ring and the glowing pit are all still present and stack up the shaft in every engine frame. The motion is still incoherent. Between ring.jpg and ring-gear-turned.jpg the gilt-mask statistics are effectively identical (hue 28.5 against 28.6, L* 43.6 against 43.5), and only the crown gear node turns (D4). The upper gear on the same shaft and its meshing partner stay frozen while the gear below them spins. The gallery's candles still give no visible glow: the brightest pixel in the upper well of void.jpg is luma 113, with no point source. There is still no chain, counterweight, piston or catwalk-level motion. The machinery now reads a little more as metal, because the gilt is less salmon (see surface), but the feature set matches the study's three-gear column rather than exceeding it.

PARTLY FIXED: the gilt gears moved from hue 23-24 to 28.4-28.9 in engine (hero, ring and void gilt masks, sat>0.3, v>0.45: hero mean 141,95,53, sat 0.62, L* 44). That is still copper/terracotta, short of #DEC16A (hue 45) and of the study's brass gears in engine.hero.png (hue 36.0, sat 0.46, L* 51.5). The gilt is also flat: L* std across the ring frame's crown gear is 4.5, against 12.0 in Blender void.high.png and 8.6 on the study's gears. It has no worn edges and no probe highlight, so it reads as painted cardboard (crop gears.png). STILL OPEN: the shaft brass still shows the crumpled-foil noise, with luma std 39.9 and p95 142 in hero.jpg against the study shaft's 30.0 and 104.3. The kerb and plinth-cap trim show the same noise (crop furnace.png). The flames are still flat triangle cards with hard straight edges. The grate bars are still near-black. The ceiling beam's side face is still a desaturated slab: sat 0.65-0.69 and L* 11-12, against sat 0.95 and L* 7 on the planks (ring.jpg, void.jpg). NEW: the pit trench is now a flat, clipped orange slab in engine. Its L* std is 1.5 (luma std 3.8) against 10.2 (27.8) in the lightmap-only frame, so the coal slats lose their gradient. Lightmap density is still 46 px/m (D5). The UV1 report shows 0 overlap px and a 20 px minimum gap. All report.json files{} hashes now match disk.

FIXED (runtime, c0dd517): the fire no longer washes to salmon. The brightest 40% of the firebox in hero.jpg measures 249,156,72 (hue 28.6, sat 0.71, R-B 177) against 254,183,73 (hue 36.6, R-B 181) in the lightmap-only frame, which was 226,161,122 at R-B 104 before. It reads amber-orange with yellow tips. The remaining 8 degree hue gap is lost green, not added blue. The deeper fire colour is by design (D6), but it sits about 10 degrees redder than candle amber #F3BE65. The pit is redder still (hue 19.6). STILL OPEN: the room reads oxblood rather than walnut and amber. Measured like-for-like (CIELAB L*, HSV, 1280x720 AgX) against the re-shot study engine.hero.png: (1) the full frame is hue 16.6, sat 0.78, L* 15.3 here against hue 20.9, sat 0.58, L* 17.8; (2) the ceiling planks are hue 7, sat 0.95, L* 7.3 against hue 14.6, sat 0.91, L* 9.1; (3) the open floor is hue 21, sat 0.72-0.73, L* 22-24 against hue 25.6, sat 0.39, L* 33.0, so the stone floor still reads orange-brown, not grey-beige; (4) the right-wall wallpaper is hue 13, sat 0.87 against 18.8, sat 0.71, though its value now matches (L* 15.1 in both). Source: the fire-tinted bake already leans red, and the runtime pushes it further than it does in the study. Lightmap-only to full frame, the ceiling hue goes 13.6 to 6.6 and the wall 17.6 to 13.0 here, against 16.0 to 14.6 on the study ceiling. Corners stay warm-dark rather than black.

rubric.criterion: readability and comfort at seated VR distance
rubric.note: Unchanged geometry, so the old assessment holds. The room has one strong central silhouette, and the moving crown gear sits 3.6 m overhead, outside the near field. The 2.3 m plinth and the 3.64 m kerb collider still split the 8 m width into roughly 2.2 m lanes either side. The open floor is darker than the study's (L* 22-24 against 33) and orange rather than grey, which lowers the contrast for brass automatons standing on it. The walls now match the study's value (L* 15.1), which helps a little. The peach plinth face (L* 41, hue 23) and the fire are still the brightest large areas and pull the eye to the furnace, not to the enemies.

topFixes: Make the gears read as polished brass in the engine, not copper card. Lift the gilt to hue 36 or above at sat around 0.45-0.55, as the study's gears measure (36.0, 0.46, L* 51.5), with the gold end of #DEC16A as the target. Add painted value variation and worn edges, plus a highlight from the probe or the bake. Engine L* std on the crown gear is 4.5 against 12.0 in Blender, so the dielectric const slot (D3) is what flattens it. Reuse the kit's brass set, and calm the foil noise on the shaft and trim (luma std 39.9 down to the study's 30 or lower).

Pull the room off oxblood. Bake the room fill with a lighter amber than the fire's (1.0, 0.33, 0.06), or separate the fire glow from the general fill, and find why the runtime shifts this room's hues 5-7 degrees redder than the study's (ceiling 13.6 to 6.6). Targets: open floor near sat 0.4 and L* about 33, ceiling hue about 15, full frame near hue 21 and sat 0.58. Restore the pit trench gradient: engine L* std is 1.5 against 10.2 in the lightmap-only frame.

Make the shaft read as endless and working. Replace the plank lid and cap disc at the top of the well with falling darkness or more shaft, light the gallery candles so they read as point glows, and either drive the meshing train at the correct ratios or stop the crown gear so the motion is mechanically coherent. Give the fire cards painted soft-edged flame shapes in place of hard triangles.
independentScore.method: I read docs/art-bible.md (palette, rendering and light) and the previous independentScore in provenance.json (69, build db29fbd), then re-checked every point it made. I read the ac21f3b and c0dd517 commit messages to learn what changed: gilt albedo, emitters taken out of tone mapping, and no geometry change for this room. I weighted the engine shots first: all eight docs/verification/p5-rooms-gear-shaft-*.jpg, viewed in full plus 2x Lanczos crops of the furnace, the gear train and the upper well. I used the review sheet and the Blender renders (void.high.png, plus a contact sheet of every staging/renders/*.png) to separate bake faults from runtime ones. The fire wash and gilt hue are runtime faults (the lightmap-only frame keeps the fire at hue 36.6 and the gilt at sat 0.88). The oxblood cast and the orange floor start in the bake and are amplified at runtime. My benchmark was the study's re-shot engine.hero.png and engine.hero.diffuse.png from the same 1280x720 harness, and I viewed p5-int-study.jpg only. Measurements used Pillow and numpy on fixed boxes, which I checked against overlay images: region mean RGB, HSV of the mean, CIELAB L* mean and std, luma std and p95, R-B, and gilt masks (sat>0.3, v>0.45). The regions were the firebox (brightest 40%), pit trench, crown and upper gears, shaft, ceiling planks, beam side face, wallpaper, wainscot, open floor, plinth face, upper well and the full frame, measured in the engine, lightmap-only and Blender frames. My L* figures are CIELAB, not the HSL lightness the previous review appears to use, so only my like-for-like study comparisons should be compared, not the absolute numbers across reviews. I verified the report.json files{} hashes against disk (all six match) and read uv1-report.json and engine-compare.json (frame_ratio 0.868, rmse 0.0262). Scripts and crops are in /tmp/rxr-score-gs3/.
